Based on the retrieved healthcare Q&A matches, it appears that women with ovaries of polycystic morphology (PCO) without other features of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) may not benefit from short-term metformin co-treatment during In Vitro Fertilization (IVF).

The clinical trial data available through Clinical Trials.gov, NCT01046032, indicate that there is no benefit in metformin co-treatment before and during IVF in women with PCO without any other features of PCOS.

Furthermore, the research on endometrial polyps from pre- and post-menopausal women suggests that they exhibit differing hormone receptor and proliferation markers, which may be responsible for their growth. However, both groups appear to have lost control mechanisms for apoptotic regulation, leading to increased growth.

In terms of prostate cancer treatment, older men with localized prostate cancer may benefit from curative therapy due to improved life expectancy and quality of life. However, the presence of endometrial polyps in these patients may not significantly impact their prognosis or treatment outcomes.

Regarding ovarian cancer, there is no clear evidence that women with synchronous primary cancers of the endometrium and ovary (Lynch syndrome) have increased risk of other types of cancer, including cardioembolic stroke. The combination of clinical data and serum total bilirubin may be a useful strategy to diagnose cardioembolic stroke in the acute phase.

Overall, it is essential for women with ovaries of polycystic morphology without other features of PCOS to discuss their individual situation with their healthcare provider, as they should consider alternative treatment options or alternative approaches based on their specific circumstances.
